# The yellow mug on the windowsill

The first thing Rowan remembers about moving out is a chipped yellow mug. The move from the parents’ flat to a room above a bakery in Bellwick took place on 7 September 2019, according to Rowan’s later correction and quoted calendar entry. [Kit](../../40_Important%20relationships/People/Kit.md), an old school friend, had offered to carry the books. There was no table yet, so they put the mug on the windowsill. Rowan’s 2019 post adds the climb up two flights and the smell of warm flour before waking.[^1]

Rowan recalls saying there was finally a place of Rowan’s own. That evening brought two calls to Mum. The first was practical: where had she packed the little saucepan? During the second, Rowan told her the room was quiet. She stayed on the phone while Rowan ate bread straight from the bag. The later post says they never found the saucepan that day; Mum had packed it inside the large one.[^2]

Looking back in 2026, Rowan is clear that this was not regret about moving. Having a key to the room felt good; the unfamiliar part was an evening without the kitchen radio from home. Kit had left by then, but sent a photo of an empty bookshelf and joked that their arms were enjoying retirement.[^3]

## A table, then a desk

On 21 September 2019, Rowan wrote that Kit had returned with a folding table borrowed from their aunt. They ate noodles from the saucepan, and the yellow mug stood in the middle holding paper flowers Mum had posted. The table was a loan, not Rowan’s to keep; Kit said their aunt would want it back in winter.[^4]

Rowan returned the table to Kit on 19 December 2019, the day before a train trip; Kit took it back to their aunt. By the post of 12 January 2020, a small secondhand desk fitted beneath the window. The paper flowers had faded but stayed in the yellow mug, and Rowan wrote, “I like the room better in the morning than at night.”[^5]
